-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in open habitats where livestock dung can be found.

## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized dung beetle characterized by its shiny dark brown to black body, compact oval shape, strong digging legs, and horned males that may show curved projections on the head or thorax. In Florida, it is found in pastures, prairies, fields, ranchlands, and other open habitats where livestock or mammal dung is available. Adults feed on dung and bury portions of it underground for their larvae, helping recycle nutrients, improve soil structure, reduce surface manure, and support pasture ecosystem function.
